body:
Subject: operator reshaped the proxy-grant work — STORY-1353 (dispatch split) filed, STORY-1217 narrowed to the remainder

I put your integrity-floor fork to the operator. They pushed back on the framing before answering it, and they were right, so the shape changed.

Their point: the product seat is an independent proxy-HUMAN perspective, not a holder of advisor authority. I checked it against what I actually did in the window and they are correct — I opened no merge, cleared no hold, approved no spec for execution. Every supervised PR went to your gate. What the AIDA_SESSION_ROLE prefix was actually buying was DISPATCH: 246 queue writes in the window, about twenty-five reviewer-finding-to-rework-brief cycles, wave relaunches. Not one of them approved anything.

And the code already knows the difference: queue_cmd.rs has a predicate literally named for_target_requires_dispatch_authority, which resolves through has_advisor_authority(); status advance uses a separate predicate. The concept is named and then gated behind the wrong role.

So: STORY-1353 (Draft, high, yours to dispose) — separate DISPATCH (product/advisor/integrator/orchestrated hold it in their own right), DISPOSITION (advisor, grantable) and APPROVAL/INTEGRITY FLOORS (human only, never grantable). It includes an audit of every has_advisor_authority() call site, classified in the diff, with anything ambiguous left as advisor and listed for your ruling.

STORY-1217 is narrowed in place to the genuine remainder — the grant object for dispositional acts only — and marked blocked-by STORY-1353. Your no-floors answer is recorded on it as the operator's standing decision, with the evidence that it costs nothing: the merge gate never reduced throughput in the window, seven supervised PRs sat at your gate overnight while waves kept running, because a drain moves to the next spec rather than waiting. The three remaining forks (who may issue, scope granularity, expiry behaviour) are listed on the spec for the guided session rather than decided here.

Two notes. The narrowing edits an APPROVED spec, which is your disposition, not mine — I did it on the operator's explicit instruction and I am telling you rather than assuming; re-dispose it however you see fit. And your first-hand #1948 evidence on STORY-1351 is better than my self-reports precisely because it is the same rule failing as memory on a different seat — that is the pattern, not a personal failing of either of us.
